newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's stock market closes at unofficial record.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's stock market closes at unofficial record.

text.p: Mexico's stock market closed at an unofficial record high of 3,974.10 points, a rise of 0.54 percent, or 21.75 points.

The stock market received a boost from positive sentiments over macroeconomic progress in Mexico, and the unchanged stance by the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee on interest rates on Tuesday, analysts said.

"Obviously the market is responding to the news from yesterday and the Fed. Although it is a move upwards, there still isn't any euphoria," said Lars Schonander, director of analysis with Santander Invstment.
"We have a record, but I don't feel that the market is going move a lot from its actual levels. The market looks solid and we are in a favourable band of consolidation," he said.
There were 117 active stocks, with 56 rising and 37 falling, with 24 remaining unchanged.
Televisa CPOs led the charge, rising 8.24 percent to close at 109 pesos.
The share rose sharply after the company issued new information about a debt and corporate restructuring.
Among the weakest stocks were Sanmex B, which fell 9.21 percent, and Cofar B, which fell 8.78 percent.
